title: Ergonomic SDK wrappers for progressive function calls with schema-validated streaming chunks
text:
Ergonomic SDK wrappers for progressive function calls with schema-validated streaming chunks

description:
Introduce ergonomic, cross-language SDK wrappers that make it easy to implement progressive (streaming) function/tool calls where each incremental chunk is validated against a schema. Goal: provide strongly-typed TypeScript + Python + Go examples and runtime helpers that preserve low-latency streaming while optionally validating structured chunks to prevent downstream regressions.

acceptance_criteria:
- TS/Python/Go SDKs expose a lightweight SessionWrapper API for streaming function/tool calls
- SessionWrapper yields validated chunk objects (or schema-validated events) incrementally, with an opt-out for validation to minimize CPU overhead
- Backwards-compatible with current event envelope (v1) and supports opt-in v2 framing header for schema chunks
- Unit/integration tests for each language that simulate partial chunk arrival and JSON streaming boundary cases
- Performance tests demonstrating <5% median token-latency regression with validation enabled on representative workloads

technical_notes:
Design decisions: use Zod for TypeScript runtime schema validation, Pydantic models for Python, and json.Decoder + manual struct unmarshal for Go to stream-parse partial JSON. To reduce overhead we propose a two-mode validator: 'strict' (full validation on each chunk) and 'fast' (light structural checks + best-effort decode). We will add a header 'x-rw-schema-v' to indicate chunk schema version and a fallback path for raw text tokens. Trade-offs: strict validation prevents regressions but increases CPU; fast mode is necessary for high-throughput low-latency paths. The wrappers will expose hooks for metrics (validation_time_ms, validation_mode, chunk_size_bytes) to feed into Console dashboards.

implementation_plan:
1) Spec: finalize event framing and header contract (PRD linked)
2) Implement TS SessionWrapper + zod schemas and examples in sdk-js/examples/stream-validated
3) Implement Python SessionWrapper using pydantic BaseModel with streaming parse helpers in sdk-py/examples/stream_validated
4) Implement Go SessionWrapper using a streaming decoder and safe-unmarshal pattern in sdk-go/examples/streamvalidated
5) Add cross-language integration tests and microbench harnesses (runtime-1.22 test infra)
6) Docs: migration guide, FAQ, and code samples for canary customers
7) Rollout: experimental flag in hosted API, telemetry opt-in, and performance monitoring
8) Ship GA once tests and perf thresholds are satisfied

updates:
2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — aligned on schema header 'x-rw-schema-v' and two validation modes (strict/fast). Assigned implementers for each SDK.
2026-03-05: Prototype TS wrapper implemented (poC). Observed ~12% CPU increase with strict validation on small model; fast mode reduces overhead to ~3%.
2026-03-09: Design review — PM asked to add migration story for customers using raw streaming envelopes; added opt-in 'schema_v2' header behavior and fallback to raw text parsing.
2026-03-11: Python pydantic streaming helper landed in branch feature/sdk-stream-validate-py (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-py/pull/62). Tests for nested arrays added.
2026-03-13: Go streaming prototype shows brittle behavior on interleaved control frames. Decided to normalize control frames to minimal single-byte markers before JSON chunks to simplify parsing; updated spec draft.
2026-03-14: End-to-end test harness being added. Preparing canary with two internal services to run traffic and collect validation metrics.

review_comments:
PM Alex Rivera: Please include migration example for clients that only consume text tokens; ensure no disruption to streaming-only paths.
Design Lara Nguyen: Small doc UI note — show clear toggle for 'Validate chunks' in Console and warn about CPU cost.
Security Samir Patel: Need threat model for schema injection and validation loops; recommend a max-allowed chunk size and CPU mitigation circuit breaker.
Eng Lead Tomasz Kowalski: For Go, prefer streaming token consumer pattern to avoid full-chunk allocation; ensure zero-copy where possible.

qa_notes:
Test scenarios to cover: interleaved control frames + partial JSON chunk, schema mismatch recovery, opt-out flow (validation disabled), Canary run under 10k RPS for both strict and fast modes. Add fuzzing for broken UTF-8 and very large chunk sizes.

notes_for_oncall:
If validation CPU spikes are observed, flip canary flag to fast-mode off or disable 'validate_chunks' globally for the canary org. Alert if validation_time_ms p95 > 200ms for sustained 5 minutes.

expected_followups:
Add example in 'examples/streaming/toolchain' showing server-side composition of validated chunks
Integrate validation metrics into per-route dashboards in Console
Customer beta: invite two large customers to test schema-v2 and provide migration feedback
